title: Harmanpreet Kaur Becomes First Cricketer to Captain 150 T20 Internationals
excerpt: The India captain reached the landmark during the Women's Asia Cup match against Pakistan in Dubai, extending her lead over every male and female captain in history.
body:
• Harmanpreet Kaur became the first cricketer — male or female — to captain a team in 150 T20 International matches during India's Women's Asia Cup clash against Pakistan in Dubai.
  • She leads the all-time list by a wide margin, with Sri Lanka's Chamari Athapaththu second at 121 and Australia's Meg Lanning at 100.
  • Her record also dwarfs men's cricket: Namibia's Gerhard Erasmus holds the men's mark at just 91 matches as captain.
  • India had already secured their semifinal berth and were chasing a perfect group-stage record heading into the Pakistan fixture.

Harmanpreet Kaur scripted history on Saturday, becoming the first cricketer in the history of international cricket to captain a side in 150 T20 International matches. She reached the landmark during India's Women's Asia Cup 2026 Group A clash against Pakistan in Dubai.

The milestone cements her position as the most enduring captain in the shortest format of the game, across both men's and women's cricket. No other captain — in any era, any country — has led a side in as many T20Is.

A Record That Stands Alone

Sri Lanka's Chamari Athapaththu sits second on the women's list with 121 matches as captain, 29 behind Harmanpreet. Australia's Meg Lanning captained 100 T20Is before her retirement, while England's Heather Knight and Rwanda's Diane Bimenyimana have each led in 96.

The gap widens further when compared to men's cricket. Namibia's Gerhard Erasmus holds the men's record with 91 matches as captain. Former India captain MS Dhoni, one of the most celebrated leaders in cricket history, led India in 72 T20Is — less than half of Harmanpreet's tally.

"Great achievement. But the key is to keep enjoying yourself on the field, and that is a key. I try to keep up with that."

— Harmanpreet Kaur, India Women's T20I captain

From Moga to the Record Books

Harmanpreet's captaincy journey began in 2012 when she stood in for Mithali Raj in an Asia Cup final. She was appointed full-time T20I captain in November 2016 and has since guided India through multiple ICC tournaments, including two World Cup campaigns and the Commonwealth Games.

Beyond the captaincy numbers, her batting record is formidable. With over 3,500 runs in T20Is at a strike rate above 108, she is India's leading run-scorer in the format. Her 171 not out against Australia in the 2017 ODI World Cup semifinal remains one of the most celebrated innings in women's cricket history.

India's Asia Cup Campaign

India entered the Pakistan match having already qualified for the semifinals with victories over Thailand and Hong Kong. The team was seeking to complete the group stage with a perfect record under Harmanpreet's leadership.

The Women's Asia Cup represents another opportunity for India to assert their dominance in the region, with the semifinals and final still to come. For Harmanpreet, who has captained through wins and losses, rebuilds and triumphs, the milestone is less about the number and more about the longevity it represents.

What It Means for Women's Cricket

Harmanpreet's record comes at a time when women's cricket is experiencing unprecedented growth. The Women's Premier League in India has brought financial investment and visibility, while international tournaments attract larger audiences. Her endurance at the top — captaining since 2012 in a format that demands constant adaptation — sets a benchmark that may stand for years.
